brief: Hungary's payment-rails layer has almost no dedicated media watchdog: appointment and reorganisation signals for schemes, acquirers, processors and ATM/POS deployers are split between one specialist trade outlet (FinTechZone, which carries GIRO CEO interviews, Mastercard market-lead news and conference speaker rosters), one cross-sector appointment aggregator (HR Portál's vezetőváltás tag), and the statutory record. Because PR coverage is thin, the highest-yield sources are structural rather than editorial: the e-cégjegyzék/Cégközlöny company register (executive-officer changes must be filed within 30 days), its commercial mirrors (Nemzeti Cégtár, OPTEN, Céginfo), the MNB Intézménykereső for the licensed-entity universe, and foreign-parent disclosure channels such as Euronet's IR/SEC filings from its Budapest-headquartered European operations. Visa's Hungarian organisation is the clearest blind spot - the term itself is search-toxic in both languages due to travel-visa noise - and no HU-language trace of Euronet or Nexi local org changes was found, so register-diffing plus careers/ATS monitoring (GIRO's karrierportal, multinational career sites) must substitute for press coverage.
